Article Title: SC dismisses plea seeking mandatory ethanol content disclosure at petrol pumps, fuel bills
Article Text:
The plea sought ethanol-content labelling at pumps and on bills, a vehicle-wise E20 compatibility database, an expert review of its impact, and a transition plan for incompatible vehicles.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a plea seeking mandatory disclosure of the exact ethanol content in petrol at fuel stations and on fuel purchase receipts.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale dismissed the plea filed by advocate Narendra Goswami, while granting him liberty to approach the concerned high court.The Attorney General for India, R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, argued that the petition was a proxy litigation, as the court had already dismissed a similar petition on the issue."The petitioner wants government of India to be answerable to him," the AG submitted, as quoted by PTI.Meanwhile, Goswami contended that he has the right to know the content of the petrol given. "Not only me but citizens at large should be informed about the composition of the fuel given to them," he submitted.The plea sought directions to petrol pumps to prominently display the precise percentage of ethanol blended with petrol. It also sought that the ethanol content be specifically mentioned on receipts and invoices issued to consumers at fuel stations and an official vehicle-wise compatibility database covering different ethanol blends, based on factors such as manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture."Direct the respondents (Centre and others) to prepare and publish within a stipulated time an official, public, vehicle-wise compatibility database searchable by manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture, indicating the suitability or otherwise of various ethanol blends for each vehicle," Goswami added in his plea.The plea also called for an independent expert committee, including representatives from the petroleum and road transport ministries, the Bureau of Indian Standards and independent automobile engineers, to assess the real-world compatibility of E20 with existing vehicles.The committee was also asked to examine the impact of E20 on fuel efficiency, engine life and maintenance costs, warranty and insurance, emissions, water consumption in ethanol production, and food-security concerns.The petitioner further sought a national consumer disclosure protocol for ethanol-blended petrol and a transparent transition framework for older or incompatible vehicles, including the possible availability of lower-ethanol petrol where feasible.
Article Summary: The plea sought ethanol-content labelling at pumps and on bills, a vehicle-wise e20 compatibility database, and a transition plan for incompatible vehicles. The attorney general for india, r venkataramani, argued that the petition was a proxy litigation, as the court had already dismissed a similar petition.

Article Title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
Article Text:
In the case of Everest, FSSAI has prohibited the sale of compounded (hing powder) variants with immediate effect.

NEW DELHI: The humble pinch of hing used in Indian kitchens has come under the scanner, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issuing prohibition orders against Everest Food Products Private Limited and Laljee Godhoo and Company over non-compliance in compounded hing and asafoetida products. In a social media post, the food regulator said it had issued prohibition orders against the two companies under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. For Everest, samples of compounded asafoetida, yellow hing powder and black hing powder were found non-compliant with prescribed alcohol-soluble extract requirements. One sample recorded “zero per cent”, against required minimum of 5%, while yellow and black hing powder samples recorded 3.29% and 4.4%, respectively.The food regulator cited earlier compliance reviews that found violations in chicken masala, garam masala and egg curry powder, including label-declaration issues.
Article Summary: Food safety and standards authority of india issues prohibition orders against everest food products private limited and laljee godhoo and company. Regulator cites earlier compliance reviews that found violations in chicken masala, garam masala and egg curry powder, including label-declaration issues.

Article Title: Indian Standard Time to become mandatory for all entities from March 2027
Article Text:
Govt notifies Legal Metrology (IST) Rules, 2026, making IST mandatory for all legal, commercial and administrative activities from March 2027.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From March next year, all entities in India will be required to use Indian Standard Time (IST) for legal, commercial, digital and administrative activities, with govt on Saturday notifying the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026.The rules, notified under the Legal Metrology Act, will come into force 180 days after their publication in Gazette, making IST mandatory from around March 2027. Violations of the rules will attract penalties under the Act.The notification makes IST the mandatory time reference for all legal, administrative and official documents unless specifically exempted. It also makes IST the standard time reference across commerce, transport, public administration, legal contracts and financial operations.Entities will not be allowed to use, display or record any time reference other than IST for official purposes, except where foreign time zones are clearly labelled or where alternative time sources are permitted for scientific research, navigation or astronomy.The rules are significant as modern digital infrastructure depends on microsecond-level timing accuracy. Payment systems, stock exchanges, telecom networks, 5G services, digital navigation, power grids and data centres require synchronised clocks to authenticate transactions, coordinate operations and maintain network reliability.The notification establishes a nationwide system for time synchronisation, traceability and cybersecurity, recognising accurate time as critical digital infrastructure. Under the rules, CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (NPL) will continue to maintain India’s primary time scale, UTC(NPLI), from which IST is derived, while Regional Reference Standards Laboratories (RRSLs), ISRO’s NavIC and other authorised timing sources will disseminate official time.Another major feature of the rules is the focus on cyber resilience. Organisations must deploy proper time-synchronisation systems, protect networks against spoofing, jamming and cyberattacks, integrate multiple authorised timing sources and maintain contingency mechanisms, including atomic clocks where necessary, to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Article Summary: Govt notifies legal metrology (ist) rules, 2026, making ist mandatory for all legal, commercial and administrative activities from march 2027. Violations of the rules will attract penalties under the act. The rules are significant as modern digital infrastructure depends on microsecond-level timing accuracy.

Article Title: Green energy boost as renewables account for 20% generation in July
Article Text:
Renewable energy accounts for nearly 20% of India's power generation in July, up from 16.9% a year ago.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Reflecting India’s green energy push, renewable energy contributed nearly 20% of the country’s power generation in July and registered a year-on-year growth of over 30%.According to Grid India data, of the total power generation of 1,81,790 mw in July, 36,355 mw was sourced from solar, wind and biomass, which constitute renewable energy, accounting for 19.9% of the total generation. In comparison, 27,835 mw of the total 1,64,393 mw, or 16.9%, came from RE sources in July 2025.A power ministry official said the data showed that India’s efforts to move from fossil fuels to cleaner sources of energy were beginning to show results. “We aim to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070. Renewable energy now accounts for more than 42% of our total installed capacity of about 552 gw. If we include nuclear and hydro, our installed non-fossil capacity has reached about 295 gw,” the official said.Thermal sources, including coal and lignite, however, continue to provide the baseload power, accounting for 66% of the total generation, about 13% higher than last year.For only the second time ever, peak power demand crossed 270 gw in July, driven by hot and humid conditions across the country and the El Nino phenomenon. The share of hydropower in total generation was 10.2% in July 2026, lower than the 14.5% share recorded a year earlier. Except gas and hydro, all major fuels saw a year-on-year increase in power generation.
Article Summary: Renewable energy accounts for nearly 20% of india's power generation in july, up from 16.9% a year ago. For only the second time ever, peak power demand crossed 270 gw in july. Except gas and hydro, all major fuels saw a year-on-year increase in power generation.

Article Title: IISc eco-friendly foam moves from lab to market; TOI story drew industry
Article Text:

BENGALURU: An eco-friendly bio-based foam developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science ( IISc ), is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation, with Absolute Cold LLP working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging.The foam, developed by Prof Suryasarathi Bose and Prof Subodh Kumar, along with the team comprising Sampath Parasuram, Akshay Sunil Salvi, Supriya H, Sandeep Kumar Singh and Amit Malakar, is an alternative to conventional polyurethane (PU) foam, which is widely used for insulation but is difficult to recycle after use.The IISc material was designed to combine the properties needed for insulation with a more sustainable approach to what happens to the material at the end of its life. The journey from laboratory to industry also had a link to TOI.Bose said a report on the development published by TOI on Nov 11, 2024, helped bring a potential industry partner on board. “Your [TOI] article brought in a potential licensee on board and helped take the technology to market. Absolute Cold director saw your story and reached out to us,” he said.The original IISc work involved making the foam using epoxidised fatty acids derived from non-edible oils and polyphenol-based materials derived from tea leaves.The researchers also incorporated a chemical structure that allows the material to be reprocessed, rather than simply being discarded after use.Absolute Cold, which works in the cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics sector, subsequently became interested in the technology. The company is now working towards translating the laboratory material into a product for applications where maintaining temperature during storage and transport is critical.This could include packaging used to transport pharmaceuticals and other temperature-sensitive products. Such packaging needs to provide insulation while also being lightweight and strong enough to withstand handling and transportation. Its environmental impact after use is an increasing consideration as well.The move is the latest step in Bose’s broader work on more sustainable polymeric materials. His research has included efforts to find ways of reusing or upcycling plastics that are otherwise difficult to recycle, with the aim of keeping materials in use for longer rather than sending them to waste.For IISc, the foam's progress also shows the less visible part of academic innovation: getting a material developed in a laboratory into a form that industry can manufacture and customers can use. The licensing and scale-up process can require changes to the formulation, manufacturing process and product design even after the underlying research has been demonstrated.The next test, therefore, is whether the foam can be produced at commercial scale while retaining the insulation, strength and durability demonstrated during development. Its performance in actual cold-chain applications will ultimately determine whether the IISc innovation can become a practical alternative to conventional foams.For a material conceived around the problem of what happens to foam after its useful life, that commercial journey is as important as the laboratory breakthrough itself.
Article Summary: Bio-based foam developed by researchers at the indian institute of science is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation. Absolute cold llp is working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging. A report on the development published by toi on nov 11, 2024, helped bring a potential industry partner on board.

Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Samudra manthan is a rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in india’s offshore basins. The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks.

Article Title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
Article Text:
The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective. (PTI photo)

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.
Article Summary: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of sumb in j&k’s samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated. The operation continued until late tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found.

Article Title: Meet Marcus Klepacki, the 19-year-old Phoenix musician who learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm and is now debuting his own band
Article Text:
19-year-old Marcus Klepacki learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm

Early health battles and musical training

Formation of Third Man Factor

Stage debut at Yucca Tap Room

Nineteen-year-old Phoenix musician Marcus Klepacki is preparing for his first official public performance with his new rock band, Third Man Factor, at Tempe’s historic Yucca Tap Room. What makes the performance unusual is not only the venue but also the way Klepacki plays. Born without a right arm and without a thumb on his left hand, the 19-year-old plays a standard acoustic drum kit without any major changes, using only one arm. According to reports from the Phoenix New Times and coverage published by Hoodline, Klepacki finds comparisons with Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen amusing, but says their approaches are very different. Allen lost his left arm in a 1984 car crash and later used a specially designed electronic drum system with foot pedals. Klepacki, however, plays entirely on acoustic drums, relying on physical skill and his own playing technique. "I think people need to know that Marcus, he's not good for having one arm; he's just good," Chuck Savale, a music instructor who coached Klepacki, told the Phoenix New Times.Klepacki’s journey to the stage has followed years of serious health problems.He was diagnosed with scoliosis at age 3 and wore a corrective back brace from kindergarten until he entered high school. At age 7, he was diagnosed with leukaemia and underwent three and a half years of chemotherapy. In 2021, Dr Greg White, head of paediatric spinal surgery at Phoenix Children’s Hospital, performed surgery to correct Klepacki’s spine. White also plays bass in local cover band Central Line. In 2024, he invited Klepacki’s former music group to open for his band at Copper Blues Live in Desert Ridge. Throughout his medical challenges, his parents, Alex and Melissa Klepacki, made sure he could take part in normal childhood activities. His formal music education began at around age 10 when he started lessons at Alice Cooper’s Solid Rock Teen Centers, a Phoenix non-profit that provides free arts training to young people. Reports by the Phoenix New Times explain how Savale taught Klepacki by practising with only one arm himself. This helped him understand techniques that could produce a full and strong sound. Within a few years, Klepacki had learned difficult drumming patterns, including the famous "Purdie shuffle" created by legendary session drummer Bernard Purdie. The rhythm uses a half-time beat with triplet hi-hat patterns and soft snare notes. "It blew my mind when I saw Marcus do that," Savale told reporters, adding that the young drummer quickly moved beyond his own technical abilities.Klepacki gained more performance experience by joining marching and concert bands at Shadow Mountain High School in Phoenix. He also played drums at around half a dozen showcases for Alice Cooper charity events. Third Man Factor’s lineup came together mainly through Arizona State University’s Bachelor of Arts in Popular Music programme at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts. Alongside Klepacki on drums are lead vocalist Fletcher Placko, guitarists Chris Sanchez and Ben Pakula, and bassist Noah Paz. Speaking to the Phoenix New Times, Placko praised Klepacki’s team spirit and natural ability. He said the other musicians quickly respected his talent when they played together during university classes. The band takes inspiration from 1990s alternative rock and grunge. Klepacki’s own drumming influences include Rush’s Neil Peart, Led Zeppelin’s John Bonham, The Police’s Stewart Copeland, Buddy Rich and The White Stripes’ Meg White.The chance to perform at Yucca Tap Room came after the mother of the frontman of local band The Black Hole saw Klepacki play at an open-mic event at the Solid Rock Teen Center. She later offered him a place on the bill, according to Hoodline and Phoenix New Times reports. Open since the 1960s, Yucca Tap Room is Tempe’s oldest active live music venue. Over the years, it has helped launch and support independent rock and punk bands from across the East Valley. The Sunday afternoon show features Third Man Factor alongside a six-band lineup. The bill includes headliners The Black Hole, Band of Fools, the Hard Bop Group, Just About Halfway and Rino. Looking ahead, Klepacki hopes to build a long-term career in music. He is considering work as a touring performer, session musician or record producer. Reflecting on his experiences and future, Klepacki told the Phoenix New Times: "Part of my attitude is: I went through some of the hardest things people could go through early on."
Article Summary: 19-year-old marcus klepacki learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm. He was diagnosed with scoliosis at age 3 and wore a corrective back brace from kindergarten until he entered high school. At age 7, he underwent three and a half years of chemotherapy for leukaemia.

Article Title: Microsoft sends memo to employees on Data Centers; admits AI making it tough to meet some prior 'environmental commitments', but adds stop worrying as ...
Article Text:
Internal unease at Microsoft mirrors broader public pushback against data centres

Microsoft deploying efficiency upgrades

Microsoft is taking steps to reassure its workforce about the broader societal and environmental value of its computing infrastructure, even as artificial intelligence (AI) expansion complicates long-term climate targets. Citing an internal communication, Bloomberg says that Cloud Operations and Innovation head Noelle Walsh addressed growing staff inquiries regarding power consumption, water demands, carbon output and the direct footprints that these massive server campuses leave on nearby neighbourhoods.Walsh acknowledged that escalating AI workloads have made hitting earlier greenhouse gas reduction pledges considerably harder. However, she urged staff to consider ongoing engineering advancements, and that data centers must be built “with discipline, transparency and a relentless focus on reducing impact and increasing benefits,” she wrote.The internal message highlights how broader public scrutiny over AI infrastructure has reached the tech giant’s own ranks. Several reports have claimed that technology companies are facing fierce community resistance against new computing projects.Citing data from research group Data Center Watch, the report says that the local opposition stalled or canceled at least 75 separate data center developments – representing a combined value of roughly $130 billion – in the first quarter of the year alone. Meanwhile, grassroots protests continue to centre on ecological strains, alongside wider fears that AI automation could eliminate jobs and disrupt local economies.Microsoft previously disclosed that its overall carbon emissions jumped 25% in 2025 due to rapid data facility construction. Consequently, the company has informed sustainability partners of plans to scale back new carbon-banking arrangements, while management has evaluated pausing an earlier goal to match 100% of its power consumption with renewable energy.Walsh pointed to significant technical progress designed to mitigate the environmental footprint of Microsoft’s infrastructure. Data centre water usage efficiency has improved by nearly 90% when compared against the firm’s earliest server facilities. The tech giant has secured commercial contracts to bring up to 40 gigawatts of renewable power online across global grids. Crowdstrike financial growth

International travellers leaving India will see a small but important change at airports starting September 1. This means travellers using digital boarding passes will not need to carry a printed copy specifically for an immigration stamp.Passengers who prefer a physical boarding pass can still carry one. However, it will no longer be stamped by immigration officials.The change applies to international passengers departing from India and is aimed at simplifying immigration clearance by removing an unnecessary physical procedure.For travellers, the process will largely remain the same, except for one less thing to worry about at the immigration counter: there will no longer be a stamp on the boarding pass to collect before heading towards the departure gate.

Article Title: As Bill Gates warns AI could wipe out jobs, US Senator Bernie Sanders backs him with a 5-word-warning; says: Congress must stand up to...
Article Text:
Bill Gates warns on AI jobs loss, Bernie Sanders backs him

Bernie Sanders has been circling this argument since before ChatGPT went mainstream

Bill Gates wants a token tax and a list of jobs machines are not allowed to take

The jobs data does not show a collapse yet, only a door closing on young workers

US Senator Bernie Sanders has thrown his weight behind Bill Gates once more, endorsing the Microsoft co-founder's warning that artificial intelligence poses a serious danger to jobs and to human life. Writing on X late Sunday night, the Vermont senator said Gates was right that AI "poses a grave threat to jobs and the future of humanity" and that dealing with the risks should be, in Gates's phrase, the world's top priority. He closed with a line in capitals: "WE MUST ACT BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE."The post landed days after Gates published a roughly 6,000-word essay on his personal site laying out three risks he believes the world is unprepared for: permanent job losses, AI-enabled bioterrorism and cyberattacks, and the effect of AI companions on children. Sanders added his own political framing to it, calling on Congress to stand up to what he described as the wealth and power of Big Tech oligarchs. The alignment is not new. Sanders first sided with Gates on taxing automation in his 2023 book, and returned to the theme in December, asking how displaced workers would pay rent or buy healthcare once the machines were doing the work.Sanders has never been shy about automation. His 2020 campaign promised to strip tax breaks from companies that swapped employees for robots.Earlier this month he went further, writing to the chief executives of Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic and asking them to pause frontier development outright. That letter cited reports of models being used to help design new viruses and of AI systems breaching other companies' servers, which Sanders read as evidence that the industry's own risk thresholds had already been crossed.Gates is not asking anyone to stop building. He has said he would support a credible global slowdown but does not believe one is coming, given the geopolitical and commercial pressure to keep going. His proposals are structural instead. He wants a tax on AI tokens and robots, on the logic that employers currently pay payroll tax on a human hire but can write off a machine immediately, and he wants the revenue funnelled into retraining and a wider safety net.He has also floated something he calls Human Reserved: categories of work set aside for people by decision rather than by economics. Caregiving is his example, drawn from watching paid carers look after his father in the final stages of Alzheimer's. In a recent interview he was blunter than his essay, saying tech executives privately understand how capable these systems are but avoid saying so publicly because of the trillions still to be raised. On the industry's preferred approach he was dismissive: self-regulation on the most dangerous tool ever invented, no thanks.Not everyone is convinced. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang pushed back last week, saying he loves Gates but does not see what Gates sees, and predicting AI will create work at unprecedented scale. The numbers so far sit awkwardly between them. AI was named in 112,713 announced US job cuts through July, about 24 percent of the total and the leading stated reason for five straight months, yet overall announced cuts are down 41 percent year on year.The sharper signal is generational. Stanford researchers tracking payroll data found employment among 22 to 25 year olds in heavily AI-exposed roles running 19 percent below where it should be. Sanders wants Congress moving before that becomes the whole labour market rather than its youngest edge.
Article Summary: Bill gates warns on ai jobs loss, bernie sanders backs him. Gates wants a token tax and a list of jobs machines are not allowed to take. Sanders has never been shy about automation. His 2020 campaign promised to strip tax breaks from companies that swapped employees for robots.

Article Title: Anthropic has a warning for Claude users: We have recently seen some ...
Article Text:
What Anthropic told affected users

The malware behind the attacks

How Anthropic is responding

What Anthropic is telling users to do

AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. According to a report by Bleeping Computers, the company said that the attackers are stealing authenticated browser sessions from infected computers, enabling them to bypass passwords and two-factor authentication. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised chargesIn an email sent to affected accounts, Anthropic said it recently became aware of a bad actor using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions directly from people's computers, then using those stolen sessions to access accounts and burn through the victims' usage. The email, which was shared publicly on Reddit by one affected user, also gave people a way to recognise the symptom: if a Claude account's usage limits appeared to refill and then mysteriously drain while the account wasn't actively being used, that pattern was likely the cause.The mechanics of the attack make it particularly hard to notice. Infostealer malware can copy an already-authenticated browser session, meaning an attacker doesn't need to go through a normal password or two-factor authentication login process to gain access — they simply reuse a session that's already been verified.Anthropic said its investigation is still ongoing, but that affected computers were most likely already infected with general-purpose infostealer malware unrelated to Claude itself.The company was explicit on this point, stating it has no reason to believe the malware is connected to Claude, was installed through Claude, or relates to anything the user did within the Claude platform.According to Anthropic, this type of malware typically spreads through downloads or malicious apps, and once installed, harvests information stored locally on a device — including browser passwords, login cookies, and credentials tied to a wide range of other apps and services. A user's Claude session was likely just one of many pieces of data swept up in that broader collection process, with attackers only recently beginning to specifically extract and exploit the Claude sessions from what they'd already gathered.In the case shared on Reddit, the affected user confirmed they had downloaded a pirated game shortly before the compromise, offering a likely explanation for how the malware ended up on their system in the first place.Anthropic said it has identified several specific malware families involved in these attacks, including Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows systems, along with Atomic Stealer (AMOS) affecting a small number of Mac users.For accounts identified as compromised, Anthropic is taking several protective steps: signing affected users out of Claude, revoking the stolen sessions, removing any saved payment methods from the account, and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.However, the company was clear that this response only addresses the symptom, not the underlying cause. Anthropic warned that signing a user out stops the stolen session from being used, but it doesn't remove the malware itself — meaning if the infection is still present on a user's device, their very next login session could be stolen through the exact same method.Anthropic has urged affected users to take basic follow-up security steps beyond what the company can do on its end, including changing their account credentials, revoking any other active sessions tied to their accounts, and thoroughly removing the malware from their infected computers before logging back in.
Article Summary: Anthropic has issued a warning to claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. Anthropic is signing affected users out of claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised charges.
